data.title: Why is Microsoft stock rallying 4% today?
data.description:
Microsoft (MSFT) stock rallied about 4% on Friday after the software giant unveiled a major expansion of its Copilot AI assistant, adding coding capabilities, autonomous AI agents, and direct access to Office applications.

The latest update is part of Microsoft’s effort to turn Copilot into a broader productivity platform for enterprise users, bringing together tools that previously required separate products.

The company is also seeking to encourage more Office 365 customers to pay for its advanced AI capabilities at a time when adoption of its flagship workplace AI product remains relatively limited.

Microsoft is embedding Word, Excel and PowerPoint directly into Copilot, allowing users to work on documents, spreadsheets and presentations without leaving the AI application.

The company also introduced new tools designed to let Copilot handle more complex tasks and operate more independently.

The move follows Chief Executive Satya Nadella’s comments in June about building a Copilot “super app” that could bring together a wider range of AI-powered functions.

Copilot adds coding and autonomous agents

One of the most significant additions is a new feature called “Code”, which allows users to create applications, dashboards and other software using natural-language prompts.

The tool is powered by the same technology behind Microsoft’s GitHub Copilot and is expected to begin rolling out to early-access customers at the end of September.

Microsoft 365 Premium and Pro subscribers will be able to preview the feature later this year.

The company is also introducing “Autopilot”, a revamped version of the “Scout” AI agent it unveiled in June.

The digital coworker will enter private preview at the end of the month.

Unlike a conventional chatbot, the agent is designed to operate with its own identity within a company directory and can be assigned specific permissions by users.

That could allow businesses to deploy AI agents for tasks that require access to internal systems while maintaining controls over what those agents can do.

Microsoft is positioning those governance features as critical to wider enterprise adoption.

“I think it's been very hard for many organizations ⁠to bring agents into the enterprise because of security, compliance and governance concerns,” Annie Pearl, corporate vice president of Copilot Product, said in an interview.

“So we've worked... to make sure ⁠that we were building this in a way that would really be able to be used in the enterprise.”

Microsoft faces an adoption challenge

The expanded Copilot offering comes as Microsoft tries to close a significant gap between the reach of its Office software and adoption of its AI assistant.

Microsoft has more than 450 million commercial Office 365 seats globally, but fewer than 7% currently have licenses for the AI addition.

The company has also until now marketed its Microsoft 365 Copilot assistant for knowledge work separately from GitHub Copilot, which focuses on software development.

That separation is becoming less attractive as the AI market increasingly moves towards products that combine multiple capabilities in a single interface.

OpenAI and Anthropic have been building products that bring together functions such as writing, research, coding and task automation.

Microsoft’s latest Copilot update appears designed to compete with that broader approach by making the AI assistant a central gateway to both productivity and software development.

The integration of Word, Excel and PowerPoint could also make Copilot more useful to existing Microsoft customers by reducing the need to switch between applications.

Cost controls target enterprise AI concerns

Microsoft also introduced new cost-management capabilities that will allow employees and businesses to gain more visibility into spending associated with AI usage.

The feature comes as companies become increasingly concerned that rapid adoption of AI tools and agents could result in unexpected costs.

For Microsoft, providing greater visibility into usage and expenses could help address one of the barriers to enterprise adoption while giving corporate customers more control over how AI is deployed across their organisations.

The company has also announced increased volume discounts for enterprise Copilot subscriptions, effective in October.

The pricing changes coincide with the product expansion and could help Microsoft encourage larger-scale corporate adoption.

Stifel sees room for further Microsoft stock gains

The Copilot expansion comes as Microsoft shares enter the latest product launch with a mixed performance for the year but a much stronger six-month run.

Microsoft stock was up about 3% in 2026 through Thursday’s close, trailing the Nasdaq and several other megacap technology companies.

The shares, however, have gained about 40% over the past six months.

Stifel upgraded Microsoft from Hold to Buy on September 23 and raised its price target to $575, arguing that the company had “clearly turned the corner” following its fiscal fourth-quarter 2026 results.

The upgrade followed strong growth in Azure and Copilot surpassing 30 million paid seats.

Stifel analyst Brad Reback expects Microsoft’s recent momentum to continue, citing his “growing sense the company can drive sustained strong Azure upside.”

Reback believes Microsoft can improve monetisation of its computing capacity while slowing the growth of expenses associated with developing large language models.

He also expects the company to benefit from accelerating business at OpenAI, one of its key partners.

The analyst said Microsoft “appears to be hitting a more sustained efficiency cadence across” chips, AI models and software, potentially leaving more computing capacity available for monetisation through third-party applications and customers.

Azure growth and Copilot adoption in focus

Although Microsoft has continued to say that AI demand exceeds supply, Reback noted that the company has “softened its messaging around the need to deploy additional capacity” for some initiatives.

That could give Microsoft greater flexibility to monetise existing Azure computing capacity rather than continually directing resources towards additional infrastructure.

Reback also pointed to the growing availability of open-weight AI models as a positive for Microsoft’s strategy of remaining “agnostic” on AI models.

Azure hosts open-weight models that can also power Copilot, giving Microsoft another route to benefit from expanding AI usage across its cloud platform.

The analyst said he was “increasingly comfortable with the company's ability to sustain” revenue growth in the mid- to upper-teens range.

He also does not expect Microsoft to require “outside financing,” citing the company’s improving “operational efficiencies.”

At the same time, Reback expects improvements to Microsoft 365 to support wider Copilot adoption.

Growing use of GitHub could provide another source of momentum, particularly as Microsoft brings coding and productivity functions closer together under the broader Copilot umbrella.

data.title: Is Elon Musk's SpaceX stock a golden opportunity after its 34% pullback?
data.description:
SpaceX stock has wavered this month after hitting the crucial resistance at $158. This consolidation has coincided with share unlocks and the upcoming Starlink v3 test. It was trading at $148.03 on Friday, down sharply from the all-time high of $225. So, is this a golden opportunity to buy the company?

Analysts are bullish on SpaceX stock

Top analysts tracking SpaceX are highly bullish on the company because of its diversified business model. Many of them believe that its ongoing challenges, including cash burn, are temporary. 

The average estimate among analysts is that the stock will jump to $227 in the next 12 months. This target is about 53% above the current level. The most bullish analyst believes that the stock will jump to $800, up by 440% from the current level. 

Timothy Hiran, an Oppenheimer analyst, believes that the stock will jump to $280, while Ryan Koontz of Needham, sees it rising to $250. Macquarie has also set a target of $250, meaning that it needs to jump by about $100 from the current level.

Elon Musk is investing Across all the businesses

Recent announcements show that Elon Musk is investing across all parts of SpaceX, a move aimed at gaining market share as competition rises. The last quarter showed that the space business had a capital expenditure of $1.17 billion, while the connectivity and AI businesses spent $1.37 billion and $15.8 billion, respectively. 

A good example of this is the planned test of the Starlink v3 next week. This version will lead to an improved service as the company seeks to gain market share globally. Starlink now has over 12 million customers who are paying a fee every month.

In a statement this week, Musk predicted that Grok’s capabilities will match or be better than those offered by other companies like Anthropic and OpenAI. This statement comes at a time when the platform is struggling as competition rises and its model remains under pressure. Data shows that Grok’sperformance lags other models by far. 

READ MORE: SpaceX stock forecast after hitting a $946 million NASA deal

Growth expected to soar

Analysts believe that SpaceX has more room for growth, especially in its data center business. It recently inked a $1.1 billion a month deal. This is on top of deals with other companies like Google, Reflection AI, and Anthropic. As a result, some top companies Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley believes that the revenues will jump to over $1 trillion in the next few years. 

The average estimate among analysts is that its annual revenue will jump to $44.8 billion this year, with the most bullish one having a target of $51 billion. This surge will then extend to over $103 billion next year.

To be clear, its free cash flow will be affected by the massive investments. Nonetheless, these investments will likely be worth it in the long run, as we experienced with Tesla. 

SpaceX stock technical analysis

SPCX stock chart | Source: TradingView

The two-hour chart shows that the SPCX stock has remained inside a narrow range this month. A closer look shows that it has formed an ascending triangle pattern, a common continuation sign in technical analysis.

The stock has remained above the 50-period moving average and the Supertrend indicator. Therefore, in the long-term, the stock will likely continue surge, potentially to the psychological level of $200. Over time, the stock will likely surge to $300 and above.

data.title: Akamai stock surges 23% on $12B Anthropic AI cloud deal: why it could double
data.description:
Akamai Technologies shares soared more than 23% in premarket trading Friday after the company announced a multibillion-dollar cloud computing agreement with artificial intelligence firm Anthropic, highlighting the growing demand for computing capacity as AI developers expand their workloads.

The agreement requires Anthropic to pay Akamai $11.6 billion over seven years for access to CPU capabilities from Akamai Cloud’s distributed AI infrastructure and software.

Akamai said the deal also includes an option for the two companies to expand the arrangement by another $9 billion, taking the potential total commitment to roughly $20 billion.

The announcement sent Akamai shares sharply higher after Thursday’s close and prompted several Wall Street analysts to raise their price targets on the stock.

Anthropic deal reshapes Akamai’s AI outlook

The new commitment adds to more than $2.8 billion in existing multiyear cloud commitments across Akamai’s customer base announced this year.

JPMorgan analysts said the additional $9 billion option could follow "a path of low resistance" toward being exercised, underscoring the potential scale of Anthropic’s future computing requirements.

Anthropic will also receive warrants as part of the agreement.

Akamai is granting warrants representing up to 5% of its shares outstanding, with an exercise price of $111.33, close to the stock’s Thursday closing price.

The structure gives Anthropic the right, but not the obligation, to purchase Akamai shares at a predetermined price in the future.

For Akamai, however, the deal comes with substantial upfront investment requirements before the associated revenue begins flowing through.

The company expects no revenue contribution from the agreement this year, followed by approximately $150 million to $300 million in 2027.

Revenue is expected to continue ramping thereafter, eventually reaching about $1.7 billion annually.

Heavy capital spending needed to scale

Akamai expects to spend approximately $5.5 billion in capital expenditure to support the agreement, including $1.7 billion this year.

The investment requirement has raised questions about whether the company will need to access additional financing next year.

JPMorgan analysts flagged the possibility, while Akamai CFO Edward McGowan did not rule out additional capital needs during a call with analysts.

McGowan pointed to Akamai’s $4.6 billion in cash and another $1 billion available through lending commitments from banks.

"If we need additional capital, we'll certainly have a discussion with our board and with our senior management team and do what we think is best for shareholders overall," he said.

The upfront spending also means the near-term financial impact will differ significantly from the eventual revenue contribution, making the pace of infrastructure deployment and customer utilization important factors for investors.

Morgan Stanley analysts estimate that operating margins on the Anthropic deal will be about 30%.

They also highlighted Akamai’s use of CPUs rather than GPUs as a potential advantage because CPUs generally have lower power requirements.

The analysts described this as "a dynamic that is not well-understood by the market when it comes to running AI workloads."

AI inference business expands rapidly

The Anthropic agreement comes as Akamai’s cloud infrastructure business is already experiencing rapid growth.

Cloud Infrastructure Services revenue increased 39% year over year to $99.3 million in the second quarter from $71.5 million a year earlier.

Akamai attributed the increase to demand for AI infrastructure, higher GPU deployments and continued adoption of its distributed cloud platform.

KeyBanc analysts pointed to the acceleration in Akamai’s AI inference business, describing its growth as "unthinkable."

The business had started with 2 to 5 megawatts of commitments in October 2025 and has since expanded to between 95 and 105 megawatts, according to the firm.

Akamai expects third-quarter revenue of between $1.105 billion and $1.13 billion, alongside a non-GAAP operating margin of 24% to 26%.

The Anthropic agreement could therefore materially alter the longer-term trajectory of the cloud infrastructure business, although the timing of the revenue ramp and the associated capital requirements remain key considerations.

Analysts lift targets but flag risks

Guggenheim raised its price target on Akamai to $225 from $190 while maintaining a Buy rating after the contract announcement.

The new target represents more than 100% upside from Thursday’s closing price.

The firm said the agreement should be profitable, although margins would remain below Akamai’s typical core business margins.

Guggenheim based the higher target on stronger projections for the outer years.

Evercore ISI reiterated an Outperform rating and a $175 price target, while UBS raised its target to $148 from $143 and retained a Neutral rating.

UBS analyst Roger Boyd said the contract could provide additional upside to Akamai’s low-teens fiscal 2027 growth guidance.

However, he also noted that the benefit could be offset by pressure on margins and free cash flow as the multiyear contracts ramp up.

TD Cowen raised its price target to $149 from $140 while maintaining a Hold rating.

Compute scarcity remains central to AI infrastructure

TD Cowen said the contract highlights the continued scarcity of computing capacity in the current AI infrastructure cycle.

Frontier AI model developers are competing for access to compute, creating opportunities for alternative infrastructure providers such as Akamai.

The firm said this allows companies such as Akamai to participate in workloads that historically would have been handled by hyperscale cloud providers or through direct leasing arrangements.

At the same time, TD Cowen remains cautious about the long-term durability of Akamai’s cloud infrastructure model.

The firm said much of the current demand appears to be driven by an acute shortage of available compute rather than permanent differentiation in infrastructure.

Anthropic’s continued growth, according to TD Cowen, appears increasingly constrained by access to computing capacity.

That shortage provides a favorable backdrop for vendors capable of delivering large blocks of infrastructure.

For Akamai, the key question now is whether the current AI-driven demand for alternative compute capacity develops into a durable business opportunity as the industry expands beyond its present infrastructure constraints.

data.title: Nasdaq futures gain 145 points: 5 things to know before Wall Street opens
data.description:
US stock futures rose on Friday as another burst of AI optimism outweighed concerns over $100-plus oil and a 10-year Treasury yield near 5.1%.

Nasdaq 100 futures gained about 0.4% or 145 points, while S&P 500 and Dow futures added roughly 0.3% each.

Semiconductor names led the premarket advance, and Akamai surged after announcing a large Anthropic cloud contract.

The move leaves Wall Street trying to extend a winning week even as investors confront higher-for-longer rate risk, Middle East uncertainty and fresh US data on durable goods and consumer sentiment.

5 things to know before Wall Street opens

1. AI is still overpowering the macro headwinds

AMD, Marvell, Cerebras and Intel were up about 2% each before the bell, while Nvidia and Tesla edged higher.

Technology and communication services have led S&P 500 gains this week, while the Nasdaq remains on course for a weekly advance.

Meta was little changed premarket but was heading for a fifth straight weekly gain, its strongest five-week run since early 2023.

Its Muse assistant has revived interest in AI inference and CPU demand, while Meta is less than 1% away from a $2 trillion market value.

2. Akamai gives the AI infrastructure trade another catalyst

Akamai jumped about 21% after Anthropic committed to spend $11.6 billion over seven years on its cloud infrastructure.

The agreement could expand by another $9 billion, while Anthropic received warrants tied to as much as 5% of Akamai’s shares.

The deal matters beyond Akamai. It reinforces the idea that the next leg of AI spending is spreading beyond GPUs into CPUs, cloud networks and distributed computing infrastructure.

3. Oil and 5% yields remain the ceiling on the rally

Brent remains above $100 after Thursday’s 3.4% jump to $106.60, while the 10-year Treasury yield is around 5.1%.

US and Iranian negotiators are still exploring a phased agreement involving the Strait of Hormuz, but no settlement has been reached.

Bowersock Capital Partners Chief Executive Emily Bowersock Hill told MarketWatch that sustained 10-year yields above 5% could compress equity multiples even if earnings remain solid.

That makes the bond market a direct test for expensive technology stocks.

4. Trump-Xi summit removes one deadline but leaves major disputes open

Thursday’s White House summit produced a two-month extension of the US-China trade truce, pushing its expiry to January 10.

Tariffs, rare-earth supplies, technology restrictions and agricultural purchases remain unresolved.

The result removes an immediate trade deadline without producing a broader settlement, giving companies more time but limited additional certainty over technology and supply-chain rules.

5. Durable goods and Fed speakers could move October hike odds

August durable-goods orders are due at 8:30 am ET, with the headline figure expected to fall 0.3% while core orders are forecast to rise 0.6%. Final September University of Michigan sentiment data follow at 10 am.

Markets assign about a 71% probability to another quarter-point Fed hike in October.

New York Fed President John Williams, Kansas City Fed President Jeffrey Schmid and Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack are all on Friday’s calendar, keeping the rate debate active into the weekend.

data.title: 10-year Treasury yield holds near 5.17% as global bond selloff continues
data.description:
The 10-year US Treasury yield was little changed at 5.17% on Friday, holding near its highest level since June 2007 as a global bond selloff extended into a second week.

The 30-year Treasury yield was flat at 5.463%, after surging to levels not seen since 2004. The 2-year note yield held at 4.899%.

The move follows a sharp climb Thursday, when the 10-year yield jumped more than 10 basis points to as high as 5.223%, and the 30-year touched 5.501%, its highest since June 2004.

Global government bonds sold off in tandem this week, with Japanese government bonds, UK gilts, German bunds and other eurozone debt all hitting fresh highs, though eurozone and Japanese yields edged lower on Friday.

What's driving the move

Federal Reserve Governor Michael Barr said Wednesday that additional rate increases will likely be needed to bring inflation back to the Fed's 2% target.

Speaking at a housing affordability conference hosted by the Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago, Barr said "In my base case, further policy adjustments are likely to be needed to ensure inflation comes down to target in a timely fashion."

He said inflation "is above our 2% target and not clearly trending toward target in a timely way," while describing last week's quarter-point rate hike as a move "in the right direction."

Barr's comments came a week after the Fed raised its benchmark rate to a range of 3.75% to 4%, its first hike in three years.

Sixteen of 18 policymakers signalled at the time that at least one more increase is likely before year-end.

Bond markets have also been pressured by stubbornly high oil prices and a stronger-than-expected economic reading.

S&P Global's flash PMI data showed US private-sector activity expanding at its fastest pace in more than five years in September, adding to concerns that inflation will stay elevated for longer.

Traders were pricing in a nearly 71% probability of a Fed rate hike in October as of Friday, according to CME Group's FedWatch tool, up from roughly 64% earlier in the week.

What investors are watching next

Investors are due to watch Friday's University of Michigan consumer sentiment report and durable goods data for further signals on the economy's trajectory.

ING's regional head of research for the Americas, Padhraic Garvey, and senior rates strategist Benjamin Schroeder wrote in a note published Friday that markets have likely already priced in most near-term rate hike risk.

"Ahead, we think that there are enough rate hike fears discounted at this juncture, and certainly enough to take care of perceived inflation risks," they wrote.

But they cautioned that yields remain vulnerable on a separate basis: "Government bond yields are primed to remain under pressure on a pure debt dynamic theory, which translates into pressure for some re-widening in swap spreads, and especially in the 10yr area."

The ING strategists also noted that Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent's debt buyback programme has had some success in easing market strain, even as yields themselves keep climbing.

"So far, Treasury Secretary Bessent's buyback programme has in fact been successful in the sense that it was followed up by tighter swap spreads," they wrote.

The Treasury bought back $4.1 billion in its latest reverse auction on Thursday, part of an accelerated buyback strategy Bessent has used since August to try to steady long-term borrowing costs.

Rising yields have already fed through to consumer borrowing costs.

The average 30-year fixed mortgage rate climbed to 7.12% last week, its highest level in more than two years, according to the Mortgage Bankers Association.

data.title: Costco stock: why a special dividend may be coming soon
data.description:
Costco Wholesale (COST) posted market-beating financials for its fourth quarter last night, which is why the retailer’s share price sits comfortably in the green at writing.

Yet, a deeper dive into COST’s balance sheet suggests it’s actually brewing something even more exciting than strong quarterly figures — at least for income-focused investors.

Versus its year-to-date high, Costco stock is currently down over 15%; but for long-term investors, that muted performance may be the very reason it’s a compelling buy after the Q4 report.

Costco stock may soon pay a special dividend

Costco received a “non-recurring” $0.15 per share boost to earnings from International Emergency Economic Powers Act (IEEPA) tariff refunds in its fourth quarter.

So it’s not particularly surprising to see it handily beat Q4 estimates.

But the retailer’s release also disclosed that its cash, cash equivalents, and short-term investments have ballooned to more than $20.2 billion — up an extraordinary 42.7% on a year-over-year basis.

That makes for a solid reason to load up on COST shares because the company has a broadly known historical playbook of paying massive special dividends every few years when cash builds up (e.g., its $15/share payout in late 2023).

Simply put, framing this earnings report through the lens of a balance sheet "coiled spring" sets up a forward-looking catalyst story for income investors.

Younger consumer is turning to Costco

Beyond the headline numbers, what was also exciting in Costco’s quarterly release was CEO Ron Vachris’ disclosure that members under the age of 40 have gone up by nearly 60% since the COVID pandemic, now representing more than 25% of Costco's total member base.

That is rather meaningful for the retail giant because its traditional perception is suburban families buying bulk paper towels.

Showing how digitally enabled sales (+19.5% YoY) and delivery partnerships (DoorDash/Uber Eats) are quietly capturing younger, urban households turns a routine retail story into a generational consumer pivot.

All in all, the influx of younger shoppers creates a “compounding growth” engine that Wall Street may still be underestimating.

While under-40 members initially spend less per visit than established suburban families, management emphasized during the call that these cohorts steadily expand their basket sizes as household income and family needs grow over time.

Paired with renewal rates lingering near record highs above 90%, this demographic expansion acts as a long-term multiplier on future membership fee revenue.

How Wall Street recommends playing COST shares

With a cash-fortified balance sheet guarding the downside and a maturing customer base driving top-line lifetime value, COST stock offers an attractive entry point before the next structural leg up.

Note that Wall Street analysts currently rate Costco Wholesale at Overweight with a bullish mean price target of about $1,081, indicating potential upside of roughly 20% from here.

data.title: The higher-for-longer trade is creating a tech divide
data.description:
The 10-year Treasury yield reached a high of about 5.2% on September 24, a multi-decade high that should, by conventional logic, compress valuations across richly priced technology stocks.

Instead, the Magnificent Seven stocks have kept climbing – decoupling from a bond market that continues to reprice higher.

The immediate spark was viral consumer adoption of Meta's new AI assistant, Muse, which triggered a sector-wide buying wave on September 21.

Beneath that single catalyst sits a broader shift: institutional investors are increasingly treating the market's largest technology companies as cash-flow havens, uniquely equipped to absorb elevated capital costs that smaller, debt-reliant growth firms cannot.

Proof of AI return on investment

Meta's (META) share price jumped more than 11% on September 21 — its best single-day performance since the market turmoil of April 2025.

The rally reversed a sharp selloff from the previous week, triggered by unusually sober commentary from artificial intelligence executives.

What changed was Muse, Meta's new AI assistant: launched two weeks earlier, its rapid consumer adoption gave analysts something concrete to point to — proof that hyperscaler infrastructure spending is starting to generate revenue, not just cost.

The surge spilled across the semiconductor chain. AMD crossed a $1 trillion market cap for the first time, capping an 185% year-to-date gain; Intel rose 12%; Arm added 17%.

The Nasdaq Composite closed at a record high, up more than 2% on the day.

Balance sheet as shields

Rates above 5% change the math for any company that depends on borrowed money.

Highly levered or unprofitable software firms face real refinancing risk in this environment.

The Magnificent Seven stocks largely don't.

Generating hundreds of billions of dollars in free cash flow each year, they fund their AI infrastructure buildouts internally rather than tapping credit markets already pricing in tighter policy.

Scale also brings pricing power, which protects margins as costs climb industry-wide.

The result is a bifurcated market: capital keeps flowing into the handful of companies that can self-fund growth, while it drains from anything still reliant on cheap debt to expand.

That divide explains why megacap technology and multi-decade Treasury yields can climb in tandem without contradiction.

A narrow market advance

The exuberance proved short-lived.

Treasury yields spiked back toward multi-decade highs around September 23, as hotter-than-expected business-activity data, crude oil breaking back above $100 a barrel, and rising odds of an October Fed hike revived rate anxiety.

The Nasdaq Composite slipped roughly 1% that session, and the S&P 500 fell more than half a percent, as the rally in chipmakers stalled almost as quickly as it began.

Capital rotated into a different corner of technology instead: cybersecurity providers CrowdStrike and Palo Alto Networks led gainers.

That pivot is telling.

Investors are not abandoning caution about rates so much as concentrating capital in the handful of business models resilient enough to withstand them — AI infrastructure one week, defensive software the next.

data.title: Bloom Energy stock forms island reversal amid Project Jupiter risks
data.description:
Bloom Energy stock is in the spotlight this week because of its role in the beleaguered data center project in New Mexico. BE dropped to $254 on Thursday, before recovering a bit to the current $267. It remains about 25% below its highest point this year, and has formed an island reversal pattern.

Bloom Energy stock wavers as Project Jupiter project faces headwinds

BE stock has slumped into a bear market this year, mirroring the performance of other companies in the AI data center industry. Its challenges have been escalating because of a large data center project in New Mexico that has faced substantial opposition from the locals. 

In a statement on Thursday, Oracle, its developer, issued a force majeure notice related to the power supply, the developer, and a unit of Blue Owl. A force majeure clause normally excuse a party from contractual obligations when events outside its control get in the way. In this case, Oracle has faced local opposition about water resources and how it will power the data center.

This announcement came as banks that provided it with capital struggled to offload about $18 billion to the market. Still, Oracle maintains that it does not expect the project to delay and that it was still on course. 

Project Jupiter is an important part in Bloom Energy’s business since Oracle plans to use its fuel cells on the project. These cells are powered by natural gas, which some environmentalists in New Mexico are opposing. 

Bloom Energy’s business is doing well

The most recent results showed that Bloom Energy’s business was doing well, with its revenue growth continuing because of the AI boom. Its revenue jumped by 165.5% in the second quarter to $1.06 billion. It had made $401.2 million in the same period last year. 

Analysts predict that the revenue growth will continue in the foreseeable future. The average estimate among analysts is that its revenue will jump by 105% this quarter to $1.06 billion. For the year, the estimate is that it will hit $4.12 billion, up by 103% from the $2.02 billion it made last year. 

This growth explains why analysts are largely bullish on the company. UBS sees the stock hitting $300, while Susquehanna expects it to jump to $298. BTIG has a target of $298, while JPMorgan expects it to hit $314.

There are risks when investing in Bloom Energy. One of them is that data center project cancellations are rising in the United States, a move that may impact its project pipeline. 

The other one is that it is a highly overvalued company, with a forward price-to-earnings ratio of 98.55, much higher than the sector median of 19. This means that the management needs to execute perfectly.

Bloom Energy stock price technical analysis

BE stock chart | Source: TradingView

The daily chart shows that the BE stock has moved sideways in the past few days. This consolidation started after the stock made a small gap on September 8. As such, it is in the process of forming an island reversal pattern, a common bearish reversal sign in technical analysis.

The stock is also slowly forming a bearish divergence pattern, with the Relative Strength Index (RSI) making a series of lower lows. Therefore, the stock will likely reverse, potentially to $200 and then resume the uptrend.

data.title: Elon Musk says xAI's Colossus 2 could more than double Nvidia chip count by year-end
data.description:
Elon Musk said his xAI business could more than double the Nvidia chip count at its Colossus 2 computing cluster by the end of the year, laying out the most detailed expansion timetable yet for the Memphis-area facility.

Colossus 2 currently runs 110,000 Nvidia GB200 chips and 440,000 GB300 chips, Musk said in a post on X on Friday.

A further 220,000 GB300 chips are due to come online next week, with another 220,000 expected in November.

A third batch of 220,000 chips may follow in late December "if we get lucky," he said.

Following an earlier buildout

Musk's post also gave an updated specification for Colossus 1, the cluster's first phase, which he said runs 150,000 H100 chips, 50,000 H200 chips and 30,000 GB200 chips.

xAI has previously said it plans to equip the Memphis facility with 1 million GPUs by the end of 2026.

If all three planned GB300 waves land on schedule, Colossus 2 alone would reach roughly 1.21 million chips, already surpassing that stated 1 million GPU target.

Combined with Colossus 1's existing 230,000 chips, the Memphis site's total would reach approximately 1.44 million GPUs by year-end.

Nvidia's GB200 and GB300 chips are part of its Blackwell generation of AI processors, built for training and running large AI models.

The GB300 is a newer, higher-performance variant of the GB200, and both chips have been in strong demand across the AI industry this year.

Part of a broader compute race

xAI has framed the Colossus buildout as central to its ambition to compete with rivals including OpenAI, Google and Anthropic in training frontier AI models.

The Memphis cluster has previously drawn scrutiny over its power demands, with reports noting the facility has required significant local electricity and water infrastructure to support its rapid expansion.

Musk's announcement lands against the backdrop of continued strong demand for Nvidia's AI chips more broadly.

Nvidia reported fiscal second-quarter revenue of $96.2 billion for the period ended July 26, 2026, up 106% year over year, with data center revenue, its AI chip business, rising 117% to $89 billion.

The company has guided for revenue of $108 billion in the current quarter, which would mark its first $100 billion quarter.

Nvidia shares closed at $224.58 on Thursday, down 0.41%, before rising to $226.04 in premarket trading Friday, up 1.46 points.

The stock's day range spanned $221.09 to $224.94, and its market capitalization stood at $5.42 trillion.

What to watch next

The pace of Colossus 2's expansion will depend on Nvidia's chip supply and xAI's ability to bring new capacity online on schedule, something Musk himself flagged as uncertain for the final planned batch.

xAI has said its Memphis compute capacity also supports AI workloads for outside customers adding a further dimension to how quickly the buildout needs to scale.

Nvidia's next scheduled earnings report due somewhere in the end of November this year.

The report will offer the next major data point on whether chip demand from xAI and other large AI buyers is translating into revenue growth at the pace the market has priced in.

data.title: Litecoin jumps 30% from its lows: can an $80 breakout send LTC to $135?
data.description:
Litecoin (LTC) could be preparing for a substantial price move as it tests a resistance zone that has limited its upside since 2021. 

A confirmed breakout above $80 would place the cryptocurrency on course for an initial advance toward $95-$100 and potentially a broader rally to $135.

LTC traded near $71 on September 25, representing an increase of more than 30% from its recent low around $50. 

The recovery has strengthened momentum on the two-week chart, but buyers must overcome several closely aligned technical barriers before the longer-term bullish scenario can be confirmed.

Litecoin briefly taps the $80 resistance

Litecoin’s recovery has carried its price back above the 20-period exponential moving average on the two-week chart, currently located near $59. 

Reclaiming this moving average is a constructive development because it suggests that the medium-term trend is improving after a prolonged period of weakness.

However, Litecoin briefly touched the $80 resistance before sellers rejected it, sending the price down to $71 at press time. 

This zone contains several major moving averages, including the 50-period EMA near $71.56, the 200-period EMA around $77.10, and the 100-period EMA at approximately $79.31.

The concentration of these moving averages makes the area especially important.

Traders who bought during previous periods may use a return to these levels to exit positions, while bearish participants could initiate new shorts in anticipation of another rejection.

As a result, a temporary move above $80 would not necessarily be enough to validate the bullish outlook. 

Litecoin would need to record a decisive two-week close above that level, demonstrating that buyers can overcome both the moving-average cluster and the multi-year descending resistance line.

Confirmed breakout could put $135 in play

If Litecoin confirms the breakout, its first significant upside target would sit between $95 and $100. This area represents an important psychological and technical hurdle that could attract profit-taking.

A clean move above $100 would strengthen the case for a continuation toward the broader $125-$135 resistance zone. From the current price near $71, an advance to $135 would represent a gain of approximately 90%.

The $135 target is not based solely on the expected size of the breakout. It is also a major horizontal resistance level visible across Litecoin’s long-term chart. 

LTC has previously experienced increased volatility and selling pressure around this region, making it a logical destination if the bullish structure develops as expected.

Nevertheless, the projected move is conditional. Litecoin remains below $80, and the collection of technical barriers in that area means the breakout has not yet been confirmed.

The daily Relative Strength Index also favors the bullish interpretation. The RSI has climbed to 79, currently in the overbought region.

An RSI above 70 generally indicates that buying momentum is strong and could encounter a rejection in the near term. 

If the rejection of the $80 resistance stands, its first meaningful downside target would be the 20-period EMA near $59. That level previously acted as resistance and could now provide support during a pullback.

A successful defense of $59 would preserve the improving long-term structure and allow Litecoin to consolidate before attempting another breakout.

A sustained decline below that level, however, would place the recent $50 low back in focus.
